source.title: Reward-Free Exploration for Reinforcement Learning
source.venue: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 119

confidence_rationale: Foundational, well-cited theory with a nearly-matching lower bound, so source quality is high. Confidence is nonetheless the lowest in this pull because the mapping is genuinely poor: the framework is motivated by amortising exploration across MANY reward functions, not by curing a cold-start pathology under one. It establishes that reward-free-then-plan is well-posed and efficient; it does not establish that a single-objective agent learns better for having explored first.
failure_signatures: The guarantee concerns sample complexity of covering an MDP so that near-optimal policies can later be computed for an arbitrary collection of reward functions. ARC-074's prediction -- that without Phase 0 the agent collapses to monostrategy -- is not a claim this framework speaks to, and a null ARC-074 A/B result would not contradict anything here.

The exploration policy is explicitly coverage-maximising, visiting each significant state with probability proportional to its maximum achievable visitation. ARC-074's Phase 0 is undirected Hebbian babbling, which carries no such coverage guarantee; the theory's efficiency result depends on the directedness that the REE proposal lacks.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A reward-free RL framework in which the agent first collects trajectories from an MDP with no pre-specified reward function, then computes near-optimal policies for a collection of given reward functions. The authors give an efficient algorithm returning epsilon-suboptimal policies for arbitrarily many reward functions by finding exploratory policies that visit each significant state with probability proportional to its maximum visitation probability under any policy, plus a nearly-matching lower bound.
mapping.ree_translation: The correct formal analogue for ARC-074's Phase 0, and the citation the claim should be carrying in place of the unverifiable 'Griffin et al. 2026' recorded in its description field (see summary.md). It establishes that a reward-free exploration phase followed by reward-conditioned planning is a well-posed scheme with provable efficiency, which licenses the SHAPE of ARC-074's proposal.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two mismatches, either of which could invalidate the transfer. First, motivation: Jin et al. explore once to serve many reward functions; ARC-074 has a single objective and claims the prologue prevents a representational pathology, which is a different proposition the theory neither supports nor tests. Second, mechanism: their exploration is directed and coverage-maximising by construction, whereas ARC-074's Phase 0 is undirected Hebbian babbling gated on residue entropy -- so the property that makes the theory work is precisely the property the REE proposal does not have. Finite-MDP tabular theory to a deep embodied agent is a further stretch.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical reinforcement learning; episodic finite-horizon tabular MDPs; sample-complexity upper and lower bounds.

confidence_components.notes: Included despite low mapping fidelity because it replaces an unverifiable citation in the claim record with a real one, and because naming the mismatch explicitly is more useful to governance than leaving the formal analogy unexamined.
